events.title: PPI (producer prices)
events.line: Treat the morning print as a question and the close as the answer: QQQ's 200-day average at 680.94 decides whether to cut, and SPY's 50-day average at 764.43 decides whether to add, while history says most PPI days end up ordinary.

note.headline: PPI after a 1.34% September jump: QQQ's 200-day line at 680.94 is the test

lines.label: history
lines.text: Since 2016-11-16 there have been 125 PPI days. On a typical one, QQQ moved 0.68% in either direction, about the same as a normal day (0.7%, or 1.0x). SPY moved 0.56% against a normal 0.5% (1.1x). PPI days have usually been ordinary days.

lines.label: history
lines.text: QQQ closed up on 54% of PPI days and SPY on 55%. Big moves came on 20% of them for QQQ (beyond 1.57%) and 24% for SPY (beyond 1.13%).

lines.label: history
lines.text: The worst reaction was 2020-03-12, when QQQ fell 9.17% and SPY fell 9.57%. The best was QQQ +3.38% on 2026-06-11 and SPY +2.2% on 2022-03-15.

lines.label: history
lines.text: Producer prices rose 1.34% in September, the biggest of the last six months. The prior months were 1.08 (Apr), 0.52 (May), -0.12 (Jun), 0.15 (Jul) and 0.47 (Aug). The 3-month average is 0.65%, the 6-month average is 0.57%, and prices are up 6.35% from a year ago.

lines.label: history
lines.text: These figures have limits. No consensus forecast is available, so 'hot' and 'cool' below are measured against recent readings. The reaction history is close-to-close and is not split by whether the number surprised.

lines.label: judgment
lines.text: The latest reading is the hottest in six months and inflation is high from a year ago, so the market goes in already worried about prices. A second strong reading would confirm that worry rather than shock it.

lines.label: judgment
lines.text: QQQ closed at 688.17 in a sideways trend. It is 1.1% above its 200-day average (680.94), so the long trend holds, but 4.4% below its 50-day average (718.46), so the short trend is broken. It is down 5.47% over 20 days but up 6.35% over 5 days, a bounce from the 1-month low of 647.05 on Nov 5.

lines.label: judgment
lines.text: SPY closed at 757.12 and is in better shape. It is 1.0% below its 50-day average (764.43) and 3.7% above its 200-day average (728.99), with the 1-month low at 733.0 and the 1-month high at 773.09.

lines.label: judgment
lines.text: Fear is normal: the VIX was 17.49 on Nov 11, down from 19.46. That reading is stale; Nov 12 isn't stored yet. The market gate is inactive. Nothing in the setup points to a panic, but QQQ has little room above its long-term line.

plans.label: judgment
plans.if: The monthly change comes in above the 3-month average of 0.65%, especially a repeat near September's 1.34% or April's 1.08%.
plans.then: The market would likely read this as producer prices speeding up again. Rate-sensitive tech usually takes that hardest (general knowledge), so QQQ is more exposed than SPY. Add nothing on the day and let the close decide. If QQQ closes below 680.94, the long-term trend turns down: trim QQQ exposure. If SPY closes below 733.0, its decline is continuing. The plan is wrong if QQQ holds above 680.94 and SPY above 733.0 at the close despite the hot print. That would mean the number was already priced in, and existing exposure stays.

plans.label: judgment
plans.if: The monthly change lands between August's 0.47% and the 3-month average of 0.65%, around the 6-month average of 0.57%.
plans.then: The market would likely read this as no new information and go back to its sideways trend. Hold exposure unchanged. New QQQ exposure waits for a close above the 50-day average (718.46), and new SPY exposure for a close above 764.43. The plan is wrong if QQQ closes below 680.94 anyway, which would show the weakness is not about PPI. In that case trim as in the hot case.

plans.label: judgment
plans.if: The monthly change comes in below August's 0.47%. A reading at or under July's 0.15%, or negative like June's -0.12%, clearly counts.
plans.then: The market would likely read this as relief: September's jump looking like a one-off, which eases rate worries (general knowledge). SPY is closest to repair. A close above 764.43 puts its short-term trend back up and is the level to add on, with 773.09 (1-month high) as the full-recovery mark. QQQ needs a close above 718.46 to confirm, with 728.0 beyond that. The plan is wrong if the early relief fades and QQQ closes back below 680.94. Then the cool number did not change the trend: cut back any adds.

note.bottom_line: Treat the morning print as a question and the close as the answer: QQQ's 200-day average at 680.94 decides whether to cut, and SPY's 50-day average at 764.43 decides whether to add, while history says most PPI days end up ordinary.
